claims.claim: Secondary endurance estimate depends on gas mass and exhaust assumptions.
claims.interpretation: The article's 7 to 10 s is its own best case (high exhaust velocity, 1,700 kg, no reserve, no thrust loss as pressure falls). B1 adopts the ten-second ceiling but sets 125 kN·s usable impulse independently; with 1,900 kg that supports about 6 s of hover, so impulse binds first. Related coverage is not independent confirmation.
claims.verification: Checked 2026-10-22: TechCity (byline 'TechCity Newsroom', 18 Oct 2026) states its own estimate of about 7 to 10 s hover, from 250 kg of gas, an assumed 450 to 650 m/s exhaust velocity and about 1,700 kg. It says this is not a Tesla number. The 250 kg is attributed to the Tesla livestream ('about 250 kilos of air') for the top, ten-thruster version. B1's ten-second ceiling is the top of that range.
claims.conditions: Reported interview / narration; no independent measurement
claims.measurementConvention: As attributed in brief; not independently measured

A viable ground stop is retained; this does not establish that aerial assistance is necessary to survive. Car styling is decorative and does not change the physical envelope.
